items.title: Read the route that makes your default subnets public
items.kills: "A new AWS account starts with a private network that you must open yourself."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Find the default VPC of the Region that CloudShell uses, and read its IPv4 CIDR block.
steps.expect: One VPC ID and the CIDR block 172.31.0.0/16. An empty list means that someone deleted the default VPC in this Region: use another Region, or stop here.

steps.text: Copy the VPC ID from the output as <VPC_ID>. Read every route in the route tables of the default VPC.
steps.expect: Two routes: 172.31.0.0/16 with the target local, and 0.0.0.0/0 with a target that starts with igw-. The second route is the one that makes the default subnets public.

steps.text: Read the default subnets: the Availability Zone of each one, and whether it gives each new instance a public IPv4 address.
steps.expect: One row for each default subnet, each in a different Availability Zone, and each with true. The account did not start with a private network.

items.title: Make a subnet public with one route
items.kills: "Attaching an internet gateway makes the subnet public."
items.read_only_alternative: This command creates nothing. It lists every route table in the Region with the target of each route: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --query "RouteTables[].[RouteTableId,VpcId,Routes[].GatewayId]" A route table with a target that starts with igw- makes the subnets that use it public. A route table with the target local and no igw- target makes its subnets private, even in a VPC that has an internet gateway attached.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Create a test VPC with the IPv4 CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16, tagged for this book and this task.
steps.expect: No output. VPC_ID now holds the ID of the new VPC.

steps.text: Create one subnet in the VPC with the CIDR block 10.0.1.0/24.
steps.expect: No output. SUBNET_ID now holds the ID of the new subnet.

steps.text: Create an internet gateway.
steps.expect: No output. IGW_ID now holds the ID of the new internet gateway.

steps.text: Attach the internet gateway to the VPC.
steps.expect: No output.

steps.text: Read every route in the route tables of the test VPC.
steps.expect: One route: 10.0.0.0/16 with the target local. No route names the internet gateway, so the subnet is still private.
steps.predict: The internet gateway is attached to the VPC. Does the subnet now have a route to the internet gateway?
steps.explain: [Attaching an internet gateway to a VPC does not automatically make your instances accessible from the internet](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-igw-attach-not-enough). The subnet has no route table of its own, so [the subnet is implicitly associated with the main route table](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-route-table-implicit-main-association). In a VPC that you create, [the main route table contains only a local route](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-main-route-table-rules).

steps.text: Fix it: store the ID of the main route table. A real VPC should leave the main route table unchanged and use a custom route table. This test edits the main route table to stay at three resources.
steps.expect: No output. RTB_ID now holds the ID of the main route table.

steps.text: Add a route that sends all IPv4 traffic for other addresses, 0.0.0.0/0, to the internet gateway.
steps.expect: The output shows "Return": true.

steps.text: Read the routes again.
steps.expect: Two routes: 10.0.0.0/16 to local, and 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway ID. The subnet is now public. An instance in it still needs a public IPv4 address and a security group that allows the traffic.

cleanup.text: Delete the route to the internet gateway.
Detach the internet gateway from the VPC.

still_costs: Nothing: the VPC, the subnet and the internet gateway have no charge. Delete them anyway, so that no unused network stays in the account.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty. Find the IDs again with describe-vpcs, describe-subnets and describe-internet-gateways filtered by the tag task=vpc-t02.

items.title: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and read the route it adds
items.kills: "Private instances need a NAT gateway to reach Amazon S3."
items.read_only_alternative: These commands create nothing. First list the prefix lists of the Region: aws ec2 describe-prefix-lists --query "PrefixLists[].[PrefixListName,PrefixListId]" Expect the name com.amazonaws.<Region>.s3 with an ID that starts with pl-. Then list the routes that use a prefix list as destination: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --query "RouteTables[].Routes[?DestinationPrefixListId].[DestinationPrefixListId,GatewayId]" A route with a pl- destination and a vpce- target belongs to a gateway endpoint. Empty lists mean that no gateway endpoint uses a route table in this Region.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Store the code of the Region that CloudShell uses. The name of the endpoint service contains this code.
steps.expect: No output. REGION now holds a Region code, for example us-east-1.

steps.text: Create a test VPC with the IPv4 CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16, tagged for this book and this task. It has no internet gateway and no NAT gateway.
steps.expect: No output. VPC_ID now holds the ID of the new VPC.

steps.text: Store the ID of the main route table of the new VPC.
steps.expect: No output. RTB_ID now holds the ID of the main route table.

steps.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 and give it the main route table.
steps.expect: No output. VPCE_ID now holds the ID of the new endpoint. It starts with vpce-.

steps.text: Read the routes of the main route table.
steps.expect: Two routes. The first: 10.0.0.0/16 to local. The second: a destination that starts with pl- and a target that starts with vpce-. Amazon S3 traffic now goes to the endpoint, and no NAT gateway exists.

steps.text: Copy the pl- ID from the previous output as <PL_ID>. Try to delete the endpoint route as you would delete any other route.
steps.expect: An error message. The route stays in the route table.
steps.predict: You can delete a route that you added yourself. Can you delete the route that the endpoint added?
steps.explain: You [cannot explicitly delete or modify the endpoint route](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-route-auto-added). To remove the route, you change the route tables that the endpoint uses. This VPC has no internet gateway, and the route still reaches Amazon S3. [Gateway VPC endpoints provide reliable connectivity to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device for your VPC](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-s3-dynamodb-no-privatelink).

steps.text: Fix it: remove the main route table from the endpoint.
steps.expect: The output shows "Return": true.

steps.text: Read the routes of the main route table again.
steps.expect: One route: 10.0.0.0/16 to local. The endpoint route is gone, although you never deleted it.

cleanup.text: Delete the VPC. If the command reports a dependency, wait one minute for the endpoint deletion to finish, then run it again.

still_costs: Nothing: the VPC and the gateway endpoint have no charge. Delete them anyway, so that no unused network stays in the account.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty. Find the IDs again with describe-vpcs and describe-vpc-endpoints filtered by the tag task=vpc-t03.

items.title: Read the default security group and network ACL side by side
items.kills: "A security group can block one IP address or range."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Find the ID of the default VPC of the Region that CloudShell uses.
steps.expect: One VPC ID. An empty list means that this Region has no default VPC: use another Region, or stop here.

steps.text: Copy the VPC ID as <VPC_ID>. Read the inbound rules of the default security group of that VPC. Look for a field that says allow or deny.
steps.expect: If nobody changed the group: one rule with IpProtocol -1, which means all traffic, and the ID of this same security group under UserIdGroupPairs. No field says allow or deny.

steps.text: Read the outbound rules of the same security group.
steps.expect: If nobody changed the group: one rule with IpProtocol -1 and the range 0.0.0.0/0. Again, no field says allow or deny.

steps.text: Read the rules of the default network ACL of the same VPC: direction, number, action and range.
steps.expect: If nobody changed the network ACL: rule 100 with allow and rule 32767 with deny, both for 0.0.0.0/0, once for outbound (true) and once for inbound (false). Each network ACL rule names its action. A security group rule names none.
